configuration.description:
The Long March 8A is an orbital launch vehicle developed by the China Academy of Launch Vehicle Technology based on the Long March 8. It has an increased capability of up to 7 tonnes to a 700 km altitude sun-synchronous orbit. It implements a larger 3.35 meters diameter liquid hydrogen/liquid oxygen 2nd stage, coupled with 2 upgraded version of the YF-75D engines used on the Long March 5 (known as the YF-75H) with increased thrust to 10 tonnes each through measures such as increased turbopump speeds. 

The Long March 8A can also use a larger 5.2 meters diameter payload fairing.

location.description:
The Wenchang Space Launch Site is a rocket launch site located in Wenchang on the island of Hainan, in China.

Formally a suborbital test center, it currently serves as China's southernmost spaceport. The site was selected for its low latitude, 19° north of the equator, allowing for larger payloads to be launched. It is capable of launching the Long March 5, the heaviest Chinese rocket. Unlike launch facilities on the mainland, Wenchang uses its seaport for deliveries.

vid_urls.title: Live: SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 24 Starlink internet satellites from California
vid_urls.description:
Watch live coverage as SpaceX launches a Falcon 9 rocket from California with 24 satellites for the company's Starlink space-based internet service. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base is scheduled for Tuesday, August 4, at 10:05 a.m. PDT (1:05 p.m. EDT / 1705 UTC).

The first-stage booster, serial number B1063, launching for a 34th time, will land on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You' nearly 8.5 minutes into the flight.

The Starlink 17-53 mission will take a southerly trajectory upon departure from Vandenberg. 

Live commentary from Spaceflight Now's Will Robinson-Smith will be provided starting about 30 minutes prior to launch.

vid_urls.description:
Watch live coverage as SpaceX launches a Falcon 9 rocket carrying three BlueBird satellites for AST SpaceMobile’s cellphone service from space. Liftoff from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is scheduled for Wednesday, August 5, at 3:42 a.m. EDT (0742 UTC). Inside the payload fairing are BlueBird 11, 12 an 13, each satellite has a communications array measuring about 2,400 square feet.

In addition to our launch coverage, we will watch for a Falcon 9 second stage to crash into the moon at around 2:35 a.m. EDT (0635 UTC). The stage helped launch Firefly's Blue Ghost-1 and Japan's ispace Hakuto-R missions to the moon in January 2025. vid_urls.description:
Launch Window: August 5th from 3:42AM to 5:18AM EDT (07:42-09:18 UTC)
Current T0: August 5th at 3:42AM EDT (07:42 UTC)

Mission: Falcon 9 launch of Bluebird 11, 12, and 13 satellites for AST Space Mobile
Launch location: Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40), Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Earth.
Target orbit: Low-Earth Orbit (LEO)
Booster: B1077-30; 49d 1h 2min 30s turnaround
Past customer missions: Crew-5, GPS-III SV06, Inmarsat-6 F2, CRS-28, Galaxy 37, NG-20, Optus-X, BlueBird 8-10. 
Past Starlink missions: 5-10, 6-13, 6-25, 6-33, 6-43, 6-51, 6-63, 10-4, 8-11, 6-71, 12-18, 12-25, 12-23, 12-19, 10-28, 10-14, 10-21, 6-95, 10-36, 10-33, 10-31.
Satellites launched: 569, will be 572 after this mission.
Booster recovery: A Shortfall Of Gravitas (ASOG)
